passages.text: “For the kingdom of heaven is like a landowner who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
passages.sermon:
The kingdom of heaven is like a landowner.
This landowner went out early in the morning.
He wanted to hire workers.
He wanted these workers to work in his vineyard.
passages.original: Ὁμοία γάρ ἐστιν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐξῆλθεν ἅμα πρωῒ μισθώσασθαι ἐργάτας εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.
passages.sermon:
The landowner spoke with the workers.
He made an agreement with them.
He promised to pay them a denarius for one day’s work.
He sent the workers into his vineyard.
passages.original: συμφωνήσας δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐργατῶν ἐκ δηναρίου τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα αὐτοῦ

passages.text: About the third hour he went out and saw others standing in the marketplace doing nothing.
passages.sermon: The landowner went out again about the third hour.\r\nHe saw other people standing in the marketplace.\r\nThey were doing nothing.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν περὶ τρίτην ὥραν εἶδεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας ἐν τῇ ἀγορᾷ ἀργούς

passages.text: ‘You also go into my vineyard,’ he said, ‘and I will pay you whatever is right.’
passages.sermon: The owner spoke to the workers in the marketplace.\r\nHe told them, "You also go into my vineyard."\r\nHe promised, "I will pay you whatever is right."
passages.original: καὶ ἐκείνοις εἶπεν Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾖ δίκαιον δώσω ὑμῖν

passages.text: So they went. He went out again about the sixth hour and the ninth hour and did the same thing.
passages.sermon:
The workers listened to the owner.
They went to work in the vineyard.
The owner went out again around noon.
He also went out around three in the afternoon.
He saw more people standing idle.
He did the same thing as before.
He invited them to work in his vineyard.
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον Πάλιν δὲ ἐξελθὼν περὶ ἕκτην καὶ ἐνάτην ὥραν ἐποίησεν ὡσαύτως

passages.text: About the eleventh hour he went out and found still others standing around. ‘Why have you been standing here all day long doing nothing?’ he asked.
passages.sermon:
A vineyard owner went out about the eleventh hour.
He saw other people standing around.
He spoke to them.
He asked, "Why have you been standing here all day doing nothing?"
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ἐξελθὼν εὗρεν ἄλλους ἑστῶτας καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τί ὧδε ἑστήκατε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί

passages.text: ‘Because no one has hired us,’ they answered. So he told them, ‘You also go into my vineyard.’
passages.sermon:
The men answered him.
They said, "No one has hired us."
The owner spoke to them.
He said, "You also go into my vineyard."
passages.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο Λέγει αὐτοῖς Ὑπάγετε καὶ ὑμεῖς εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα

passages.text: When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his foreman, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last ones hired and moving on to the first.’
passages.sermon:
The owner of the vineyard spoke to his foreman.
It was evening.
He gave a command to his foreman.
He said, "Call the workers."
He said, "Pay them their wages."
He said, "Begin with the last workers hired."
He said, "Then pay the first workers hired."
passages.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης λέγει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τῷ ἐπιτρόπῳ αὐτοῦ Κάλεσον τοὺς ἐργάτας καὶ ἀπόδος αὐτοῖς τὸν μισθόν ἀρξάμενος ἀπὸ τῶν ἐσχάτων ἕως τῶν πρώτων

passages.text: The workers who were hired about the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius.
passages.sermon: The workers came.\r\nThese workers were hired at about the eleventh hour.\r\nEach worker received a denarius.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ περὶ τὴν ἑνδεκάτην ὥραν ἔλαβον ἀνὰ δηνάριον

passages.text: So when the original workers came, they assumed they would receive more. But each of them also received a denarius.
passages.sermon:
The first workers came.
These workers were hired at the start of the day.
They thought they would receive more pay.
Each of them received one denarius.
The owner gave them the same wage as the others.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες οἱ πρῶτοι ἐνόμισαν ὅτι πλεῖον λήμψονται καὶ ἔλαβον τὸ ἀνὰ δηνάριον καὶ αὐτοί

passages.text: On receiving their pay, they began to grumble against the landowner.
passages.sermon: The workers received their pay.\r\nThey grumbled against the landowner.
passages.original: Λαβόντες δὲ ἐγόγγυζον κατὰ τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου

passages.text: ‘These men who were hired last worked only one hour,’ they said, ‘and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden and the scorching heat of the day.’
passages.sermon:
The first workers spoke to the landowner.
They said, "These men were hired last."
They worked only one hour.
You made them equal to us.
We carried the burden of the day.
We worked through the scorching heat."
passages.original: λέγοντες Οὗτοι οἱ ἔσχατοι μίαν ὥραν ἐποίησαν καὶ ἴσους αὐτοὺς ἡμῖν ἐποίησας τοῖς βαστάσασι τὸ βάρος τῆς ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν καύσωνα

passages.text: But he answered one of them, ‘Friend, I am not being unfair to you. Did you not agree with me on one denarius?
passages.sermon:
The landowner spoke to one of the workers.
He said, "Friend, I am not being unfair to you."
You agreed with me to work for one denarius.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ἑνὶ αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἑταῖρε οὐκ ἀδικῶ σε οὐχὶ δηναρίου συνεφώνησάς μοι

passages.text: Take your pay and go. I want to give this last man the same as I gave you.
passages.sermon:
The landowner spoke to the worker.
He said, "Take your pay."
He told him, "Go."
He said, "I want to give this last man the same as I gave you."
passages.original: ἆρον τὸ σὸν καὶ ὕπαγε θέλω δὲ τούτῳ τῷ ἐσχάτῳ δοῦναι ὡς καὶ σοί

passages.text: Do I not have the right to do as I please with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am generous?’
passages.sermon:
The landowner spoke to the worker.
The landowner owned the money.
The landowner said, “I have the right to do what I want with my own things.”
The landowner asked, “Are you envious because I am generous?”
passages.original: ἢ οὐκ ἔξεστίν μοι ὃ θέλω ποιῆσαι ἐν τοῖς ἐμοῖς ἢ ὁ ὀφθαλμός σου πονηρός ἐστιν ὅτι ἐγὼ ἀγαθός εἰμι

passages.text: So the last will be first, and the first will be last.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus explained a truth about God’s kingdom.
God treats people with unexpected fairness and generosity.
Those who seem unimportant now will become important.
Those who seem important now may become unimportant.
The last will be first.
The first will be last.
passages.original: Οὕτως ἔσονται οἱ ἔσχατοι πρῶτοι καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι ἔσχατοι

passages.text: As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, He took the twelve disciples aside and said, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes. They will condemn Him to death and will deliver Him over to the Gentiles to be mocked and flogged and crucified. And on the third day He will be raised to life.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was going up to Jerusalem.
Jesus took the twelve disciples aside.
Jesus spoke to them privately on the road.
Jesus said, “Look, we are going up to Jerusalem.
The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes.
They will condemn Him to death.
They will deliver Him to the Gentiles.
The Gentiles will mock Him.
The Gentiles will flog Him.
The Gentiles will crucify Him.
On the third day, He will be raised to life.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναβαίνων ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα παρέλαβεν τοὺς δώδεκα μαθητὰς κατ’ ἰδίαν καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἰδοὺ ἀναβαίνομεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδοθήσεται τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ γραμματεῦσιν καὶ κατακρινοῦσιν αὐτὸν εἰς θανάτῳ καὶ παραδώσουσιν αὐτὸν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν εἰς τὸ ἐμπαῖξαι καὶ μαστιγῶσαι καὶ σταυρῶσαι καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται

passages.text: Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons and knelt down to make a request of Him.
passages.sermon:
The mother of the sons of Zebedee came to Jesus.
She brought her two sons with her.
She knelt before Jesus.
She wanted to ask Jesus for something.
passages.original: Τότε προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου μετὰ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῆς προσκυνοῦσα καὶ αἰτοῦσά τι ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: “What do you want?” He inquired. She answered, “Declare that in Your kingdom one of these two sons of mine may sit at Your right hand, and the other at Your left.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
He said, “What do you want?”
She answered Jesus.
She said, “Say that these two sons of mine may sit in Your kingdom.”
She asked that one son sit at Jesus’ right hand.
She asked that the other son sit at Jesus’ left hand.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῇ Τί θέλεις Λέγει αὐτῷ Εἰπὲ ἵνα καθίσωσιν οὗτοι οἱ δύο υἱοί μου εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν σου καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων σου ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ σου

passages.text: “You do not know what you are asking,” Jesus replied. “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?” “We can,” the brothers answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus replied to the mother and her sons.
He said, “You do not know what you are asking.”
He asked them, “Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?”
The two brothers answered Jesus.
They said, “We can.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε δύνασθε πιεῖν τὸ ποτήριον ὃ ἐγὼ μέλλω πίνειν Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Δυνάμεθα

passages.text: “You will indeed drink My cup,” Jesus said. “But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom My Father has prepared them.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the two brothers.
He said, “You will drink my cup.
But I cannot give you the places at my right and my left.
My Father has prepared those places for certain people.
Only those people will sit there.”
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς Τὸ μὲν ποτήριόν μου πίεσθε τὸ δὲ καθίσαι ἐκ δεξιῶν μου καὶ ἐξ εὐωνύμων οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν τοῦτο δοῦναι ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου

passages.text: When the ten heard about this, they were indignant with the two brothers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus had twelve disciples.
Two brothers among the disciples asked Jesus for special positions.
The other ten disciples heard about this request.
The ten disciples became angry with the two brothers.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ δέκα ἠγανάκτησαν περὶ τῶν δύο ἀδελφῶν

passages.text: But Jesus called them aside and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus called His disciples to Him.
He spoke to them.
He said, “You know something about the Gentiles.
Their rulers act with power over them.
Their leaders use authority over them.”
passages.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς προσκαλεσάμενος αὐτοὺς εἶπεν Οἴδατε ὅτι οἱ ἄρχοντες τῶν ἐθνῶν κατακυριεύουσιν αὐτῶν καὶ οἱ μεγάλοι κατεξουσιάζουσιν αὐτῶν

passages.text: It shall not be this way among you. Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant, and whoever wants to be first among you must be your slave— just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve, and to give His life as a ransom for many.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He said, “You must not act like the rulers of the Gentiles.
You must not seek power over others.
If someone among you wants to be great, he must become your servant.
If someone among you wants to be first, he must become your slave.
The Son of Man is Jesus.
Jesus did not come to be served.
Jesus came to serve others.
Jesus came to give His life as a ransom for many people.”
passages.original: οὐχ οὕτως ἔσται ἐν ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ὃς ἐὰν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν μέγας γενέσθαι ἔσται ὑμῶν διάκονος καὶ ὃς ἂν θέλῃ ἐν ὑμῖν εἶναι πρῶτος ἔσται ὑμῶν δοῦλος ὥσπερ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου οὐκ ἦλθεν διακονηθῆναι ἀλλὰ διακονῆσαι καὶ δοῦναι τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ λύτρον ἀντὶ πολλῶν

passages.text: As they were leaving Jericho, a large crowd followed Him.
passages.sermon: Jesus was leaving Jericho.\r\nA large crowd followed Him.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐκπορευομένων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Ἰεριχὼ ἠκολούθησεν αὐτῷ ὄχλος πολύς

passages.text: And there were two blind men sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
passages.sermon:
Two blind men sat beside the road.
They heard that Jesus was passing by.
They cried out.
They said, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
passages.original: καὶ ἰδοὺ δύο τυφλοὶ καθήμενοι παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Ἰησοῦς παράγει ἔκραξαν λέγοντες Κύριε ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς υἱὸς Δαυίδ

passages.text: The crowd admonished them to be silent, but they cried out all the louder, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
passages.sermon:
A large crowd followed Jesus as He left Jericho.
Two blind men sat beside the road.
The crowd told the blind men to be quiet.
The blind men did not stay silent.
They cried out even louder.
They said, “Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ὄχλος ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα σιωπήσωσιν οἱ δὲ μεῖζον ἔκραξαν λέγοντες Κύριε ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς υἱὸς Δαυίδ

passages.text: Jesus stopped and called them. “What do you want Me to do for you?” He asked.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was walking by.
Two blind men sat beside the road.
Jesus stopped.
He called to the two blind men.
Jesus spoke to them.
He asked, “What do you want Me to do for you?”
passages.original: Καὶ στὰς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐφώνησεν αὐτοὺς καὶ εἶπεν Τί θέλετε ποιήσω ὑμῖν

passages.text: “Lord,” they answered, “let our eyes be opened.”
passages.sermon: Two blind men spoke to Jesus.\r\nThey said, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.”
passages.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κύριε ἵνα ἀνοιγῶσιν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἡμῶν

passages.text: Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus felt compassion.
Jesus touched their eyes.
They immediately received their sight.
They followed Jesus.
passages.original: Σπλαγχνισθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἥψατο τῶν ὀμμάτων αὐτῶν καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέβλεψαν καὶ ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ
